tagline: Congo's Atlantic seaboard, anchored by the oil-port city of Pointe-Noire on its headland and wild coast.
summary: The Republic of the Congo meets the Atlantic on a short but economically vital coastline centred on Pointe-Noire, the country's principal port, oil capital and coastal terminus of the Congo-Ocean Railway. The coast pairs a sheltered port bay with the long ocean beach of the Côte Sauvage and the northern beaches and cliffs around Pointe-Indienne and Diosso. The oil economy concentrates business and expatriate movement, while leisure and coastal access run entirely on roads today.
why_marine_mobility: A headland-and-bay geography, a concentrated oil-economy travel base, and a leisure coast reachable only by road make Pointe-Noire a natural setting for a scheduled water tier that links the port, the beaches and coastal industry points faster than the road network.

demand_signals.note: Pointe-Noire concentrates Congo's oil-industry corporate, expatriate and offshore-support travel.

demand_signals.note: Headland and bay geography make several coastal points slow to reach overland.

use_cases.title: Oil-support transfer
use_cases.body: Fast, reliable transfers for corporate and offshore-support staff around the port bay and coast.

use_cases.title: Headland-bypass hop
use_cases.body: Water hops bypass the road detours the cape geography forces on overland trips.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: Suited to sheltered bay hops and the ~11nm coastal run to Pointe-Indienne, where short legs and calm bay water favour a fast, quiet craft holding a schedule.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: Reserved for longer coastal extensions toward the Kouilou river mouth, where range matters more than frequency.

signature_routes: Pointe-Noire Bay ↔ Pointe-Indienne — coastal cape link
Port bay ↔ Côte Sauvage beachfront — signature-beach bay hop
Oil-support transfer hop — port bay to coastal industry points
transit_planning: National transport investment centres on the port, the Congo-Ocean rail line and the coastal road; passenger water transport is undeveloped, leaving space for a scheduled, bookable tier.
competitive_landscape: No organised passenger-vessel operator serves the coast; the bay and beaches are road-only, so a clean foiling tier opens a new mode rather than displacing an incumbent.
regulatory_note: Maritime transport falls under Congo's merchant-marine and port authority (PAPN); passenger-vessel licensing and coastal navigation rules frame a scheduled service.
seasonality: A long dry season (roughly May-September) with cool Benguela-influenced waters and a warmer, wetter season either side; the sheltered bay supports year-round operation while ocean legs are day-windowed.

precedents.why_it_matters: Durable willingness-to-pay for fast, reliable transfer a premium water tier can capture.
Leisure demand funnelled onto roads that a direct water link serves faster.
